question: If 6 men and 8 boys can do a piece of work in 10 days while 26 men and 48 boys can do the same work in 2 days, then the time taken by 10 men and 20 boys for doing the same piece of work will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate total work: 10(6M + 8B) = 2(26M + 48B) ⇒ 60M + 80B = 52M + 96B.

This gives 8M = 16B ⇒ **1 Man = 2 Boys**.

Total Work in terms of boys: (6 × 2 + 8) × 10 = 200 units.

Required Group efficiency: 10M + 20B = (10 × 2 + 20) = 40 units.

Time Taken = 200 ÷ 40 = 5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: (6 Men + 8 Boys) can do work in 10 days.

Case 2: (26 Men + 48 Boys) can do work in 2 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time ⇒ (M₁ × D₁) = (M₂ × D₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 10 × (6M + 8B) = 2 × (26M + 48B)

⇒ 60M + 80B = 52M + 96B

⇒ 60M − 52M = 96B − 80B

⇒ 8M = 16B ⇒ 1M = 2B

⇒ Total Work = (6 × 2B + 8B) × 10 = (12B + 8B) × 10 = 200B

⇒ Required Time for (10M + 20B) = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of (10M + 20B)

⇒ Time = 200B ÷ (10 × 2B + 20B)

⇒ Time = 200B ÷ 40B

⇒ Time = 5 days

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Man-Days Concept

The total work is always constant for a specific task; if the number of people increases, the time taken decreases proportionally (M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂).

Efficiency Ratio

When different categories (men, women, boys) work together, always find the efficiency ratio (e.g., 1M = 2B) to convert the entire group into a single unit.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by each individual or group, which is a product of their efficiency and time spent.</p
